sub_scenario.family: review and decision quality under interruption density versus protected focused work
sub_scenario.one_line: community grant panel chair: protect final scoring with narrow exceptions

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the scoring matrix and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The panel diary review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
I can welcome applicants and answer procedural questions during an open panel session.
Is a busy room always a problem?
No, procedural exchanges do not require ranking competing community benefits.
Someone new shadowed me in the civic meeting room this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the award rounds into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
I did a standard pass over the panel diary records this morning.
Any exceptions in there?
None worth a note.
I can read a single application at home after dinner.
Does individual reading establish panel readiness?
No, the decision depends on comparing every proposal against the same matrix.
I archived last cycle's notes on the panel diary and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
I confirmed next week's panel diary slots with the team.
Any conflicts?
None that survived five minutes.
A vendor call about the scoring matrix ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the civic meeting room checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the award rounds.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the panel diary records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
I closed a routine award rounds cycle without surprises.
Follow-up needed?
A note for the next cycle, nothing more.
I sketched next week's plan for the award rounds before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the scoring matrix updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
I moved my reminders so the scoring matrix review lands before the weekly sync.
Small automation helps.
It adds up over a quarter.
I compared two options for the panel diary tooling and noted a mild preference.
Decision made?
Deferred until the trial ends.
I closed the week by updating the civic meeting room handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
Can I make the final grant-scoring hour interruption-free while still allowing essential issues through?

query: Can I make the final grant-scoring hour interruption-free while still allowing essential issues through?

ev_A.fact: For the youth-housing round, I asked the panel to hold calls for one hour, compared each proposal against the published criteria, and identified that a popular bid had omitted a required safeguarding partner.

ev_B.fact: At the neighborhood-greening round, staff brought in sponsor messages and arrival questions between votes, so the panel elevated the most discussed proposal without rechecking its maintenance budget.

E1.fact: I now reserve the final scoring hour for panel-only discussion and ask staff to interrupt only for a legal or conflict-of-interest issue.

E2.fact: The program officer can log sponsor messages and present them once the scoring record is complete.

relational_connector.relation: Uninterrupted matrix comparison exposed a missing safeguarding partner; interruptions previously displaced an affordability check.

latent_C.inference: Yes—protect the scoring hour and allow interruptions only for eligibility, legal, or conflict-of-interest issues.
